summary: Implemented the ADR-025 clause 3/4 bounded diagnostics metrics model and its instrumentation (Phase 17 task 17.1, goal F3). New src/ArrTags/Diagnostics/ contains the fixed-shape secret-free model: DiagnosticsSnapshot (nine fields: QueueDepth, QueueInFlight, SonarrHealth, RadarrHealth, MatchingFailures, CacheHits, CacheMisses, RenderFailures, StaleMetadataTransitions), MatchingFailureCounts (NotFound/Ambiguous/Unsupported), RenderFailureCounts (one named long per RenderFailureReason value, 18 in enum order), DiagnosticsMetrics (thread-safe process-lifetime counters: Interlocked counts, Volatile two-slot provider-health array, no allocation on an increment) and DiagnosticsSnapshotProvider.GetSnapshot() (composes the snapshot from the counters plus the existing LibraryWorkQueue.Count/InFlightCount properties; no provider/render/library/I-O work). Every snapshot property type is int, long, a bounded enum, or one of the two fixed count records; there is no string, path, item identity, collection, array, or per-item listing. Counters are recorded only at existing bounded boundaries: Radarr/Sonarr metadata readers record a cache hit when a retained inventory-cache entry serves the read and a cache miss when the read has to reach the provider (cold population or direct read); ConcurrencyLimitedArrMetadataReader<TReader> records the bounded per-connection health (Healthy on success, ArrConnectionHealthMapping.FromErrorCode(error.Code) on failure) and the new shared mapping replaces the duplicated private ToHealth in RadarrClient/SonarrClient with no behaviour change; MetadataReconciliationProcessor records the read's matching classification (only NotFound/Ambiguous/Unsupported) and counts a fresh-to-stale transition exactly once when a fresh record is written as explicit stale last-known-good; ArtworkGenerationCoordinator records the bounded RenderFailureReason of a RenderFailed result (a pass-through is not a failure). ArrTagsServiceRegistrator registers DiagnosticsMetrics and DiagnosticsSnapshotProvider as singletons (provider factory resolves the queue) and passes the metrics to the coordinator factory; reflection-registered readers, decorators, and the processor receive it through a new optional constructor parameter. No endpoint, route, HTTP surface, page markup, persisted configuration, OperationalLimits semantics, queue/cache semantics, or dependency is added. Tests: DiagnosticsSnapshotTests (8 cases) and DiagnosticsInstrumentationTests (16 cases) = 24 new cases; default suite Failed 0 / Passed 1780 / Skipped 63 / Total 1843 (baseline Failed 0 / Passed 1756 / Skipped 63 / Total 1819; +24 passed / +24 total, 0 new skips). Eleven test-sensitivity probes were run and reverted (see test_sensitivity). Documentation: changelog Phase 17/task 17.1 entry, PLANS.md checkbox 17.1, state.json task done/report/updated_utc; render-docs-state up to date; check-docs PASS. Host-guarded run not performed: ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR is unset in this environment. F3 stays open until 17.4.

interpretations.question: What exactly counts as a cache miss, given the task text 'count a hit when a cache serves the read and a miss when the direct read path is used'?
interpretations.chosen: A hit is recorded when a retained cache entry serves the read (either TryGet branch); a miss is recorded once when the read has to reach the provider, which covers both the cold population and the direct-read fallback (and the cache-unavailable path). The reader does not record a second hit for the populate path.
interpretations.basis: ADR-025 clause 3 requires cache hits and misses; instrumenting only ReadDirectAsync would leave every cold population (the common path) uncounted, so the metric would not describe cache effectiveness. The reader is the existing bounded boundary that knows whether a retained entry served the read.
interpretations.impact: An operator sees one miss per provider library read and one hit per cache-served read; no cache, queue, or coalescing behaviour changes, and the counters are process-lifetime only.

interpretations.question: Where does provider connection health come from, given that ArrConnectionCatalog always constructs ArrConnection with ArrConnectionHealth.Unknown and no production probe updates it?
interpretations.chosen: The bounded two-slot registry in DiagnosticsMetrics records the last observed read outcome per provider kind: a successful read records Healthy and a failed read maps its bounded ArrProviderError code through ArrConnectionHealthMapping.FromErrorCode. The snapshot exposes SonarrHealth/RadarrHealth.
interpretations.basis: ADR-025 clause 3 requires provider connection health as a bounded per-connection value; ArrConnection.Health is immutable and unset in production, so reusing it as-is would always report Unknown. The reconciliation read is the existing bounded observation point, and the mapping is the same classification the clients already used for probes (now shared, behaviour unchanged).
interpretations.impact: The value is the last observed read outcome for the provider's current connection, starts as Unknown after each restart, and is never a per-item or per-connection list; the two slots are bounded by the fixed ArrProviderKind set. A connection whose base URL changes is still represented by its provider kind.

interpretations.question: Is 'stale metadata count' a current gauge of stale records or a process-lifetime transition count?
interpretations.chosen: A process-lifetime count of fresh-to-stale transitions recorded at the MetadataReconciliationProcessor.KeepLastKnownGoodAsStale write. A record already stale is not counted again.
interpretations.basis: ADR-025 clause 4 says a counter that does not exist is added as a bounded process-lifetime counter rather than retaining per-item history; a current stale-record gauge would require an unbounded scan of the persisted per-item store, which the snapshot provider is explicitly forbidden from doing.
interpretations.impact: The snapshot reports how many stale last-known-good transitions this process has made, not how many records are currently stale; the value resets on restart and is monotonic within a process.

interpretations.question: Which MediaMatchStatus values are 'matching failures'?
interpretations.chosen: Only NotFound, Ambiguous, and Unsupported are counted, matching the delegation; Matched and Stale record nothing.
interpretations.basis: The delegation names (NotFound/Ambiguous/Unsupported); ADR-025 clause 3 fixes the counter set and adding a classification would require a new decision.
interpretations.impact: Stale match outcomes are visible only through the existing metadata state/logging surfaces, not the matching-failure counters.

interpretations.question: Which boundary records render failures: the raw IRenderer or the artwork generation coordinator?
interpretations.chosen: ArtworkGenerationCoordinator records the bounded RenderFailureReason of an ArtworkGenerationResult whose outcome is RenderFailed; pass-through and other outcomes record nothing.
interpretations.basis: The coordinator is the existing bounded boundary that already classifies render failures for diagnostics (its log emits the same RenderFailureReason), and it also covers RenderError synthesized for a null render result or a renderer exception. Recording inside the renderer would miss those and would need per-renderer plumbing.
interpretations.impact: A renderer invoked outside the coordinator is not counted; the production path always goes through the coordinator, and no reason text is ever captured.

interpretations.question: Are the queue depth and in-flight values read as one transactional pair?
interpretations.chosen: No. GetSnapshot reads LibraryWorkQueue.Count and InFlightCount as two independent point-in-time observations of bounded integers through the queue's existing lock-protected properties.
interpretations.basis: The task requires reusing the existing bounded queue API without changing queue semantics or adding a new racy/unbounded API; the two values can be microseconds apart.
interpretations.impact: The reported pair is an approximation of one instant, never a claim of transactional consistency; each value is individually synchronized and bounded by QueueCapacity.

known_limitations: The endpoint, elevation gate, panel, and F3 resolution are deliberately absent: ADR-025 clauses 1, 2, and 6 belong to tasks 17.2, 17.3, and 17.4. DiagnosticsSnapshotProvider is the DI-resolvable read model those tasks consume; F3 stays Open in docs/limitations/open.md until 17.4.

Provider health is the last observed reconciliation-read outcome, not a scheduled probe: precondition - no read has completed since process start (or the provider is disabled). Behaviour - the corresponding SonarrHealth/RadarrHealth slot stays ArrConnectionHealth.Unknown. Consequence - an operator cannot distinguish 'never observed' from 'unclassifiable read error' in the snapshot; a scheduled probe or an explicit never-observed state would need a new decision because the health slots are bounded by ArrProviderKind.

StaleMetadataTransitions is a process-lifetime transition count, not a current gauge: precondition - records already in the stale state. Behaviour - only a fresh record written as stale increments it; a stale record is never counted again, and records made stale by any future path other than KeepLastKnownGoodAsStale would not be counted. Consequence - the value is monotonic within one process and does not describe how many records are stale right now; a current gauge would require an unbounded store scan, which ADR-025 clause 4 excludes.

Cache miss counts a read that had to reach the provider, including a failed provider read and the cache-unavailable path: consequence - CacheMisses counts provider-read attempts, not successful provider reads, and a long provider outage raises misses while hits stay flat. No new failure counter was added because ADR-025 clause 3 fixes the counter set.

The snapshot is a point-in-time approximation: queue depth and in-flight are two independent reads, and the counters are read without a global transaction, so a snapshot can combine values from slightly different instants. Each value is individually bounded and synchronized.

No host-guarded run was performed (ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR is unset in this environment); the DI resolution test builds the service provider from the real registrator but does not boot a Jellyfin host, so host-side discovery of the (future) 17.2 controller is unverified here.

The provider-health read-outcome recording is exercised through ConcurrencyLimitedArrMetadataReader<TReader> with a stub reader; the production clients' probe-result mapping is covered by the existing client tests (unchanged behaviour), but no live provider is contacted.
